text:
<meta>continues from previous page: ...The creator Mind, indeed, together with</meta> the Word, containing the circles, and turning its mechanism with rapid swiftness, bent it toward itself, and ordained it to revolve from a beginning without beginning to an end without end. For it always begins there where it ceases. Of all these, indeed, the circuit is as the mind itself willed, and it fashioned from the lower elements animals devoid of reason, for it did not provide them with reason. The air brought forth winged creatures, and the water brought forth swimming creatures. Water and earth were also distinguished from each other in the manner that had pleased the mind. The earth later brought forth the living creatures it had held within: namely, quadrupeds, reptiles, and wild beasts, both of the field and of the home. But the father of all things, being life and splendor, begat man similar to himself, and he delighted in him as in his own son. For he was beautiful, and he bore the image of his own father. For God, indeed, truly delighted in his own proper form, and granted all his works for human use. But man, <margin>note the sin of the philosophers <unclear>what it may be</unclear></margin> when he had contemplated the procreation of all things in his father, he himself also wished to construct. Whence he fell from the contemplation of the father to the sphere of generation. And although he had power over all things within himself, he noticed the handiwork of the seven governors. These, however, rejoicing in the meditation of the human mind, each of them [is] a participant of their own order.

<summary>This passage describes the creation of the animal kingdom from the lower elements and the unique birth of man, created in the image of God to hold dominion over the material world. It also marks the beginning of man's descent from divine contemplation into the sphere of generation after witnessing the governance of the celestial spheres.</summary>
<keywords>Hermes Trismegistus, creation, intellect, man, divine image, sphere of generation, seven governors, fate</keywords>

flags.english: each bestowed upon him a part of their own order
flags.problem: The Latin says they are participants of their own order, not that they bestowed it.
flags.correct: each of them [is] a participant of their own order
